items.label: STL Technology annual report: 2025 Annual Report (05-27-2026)
items.signal_prefix: Capex and capacity: no material capital expenditure in 2025

set.signal: Capex and capacity: no material capital expenditure in 2025 (property, plant and equipment rose 45.09% to NT$129,502 thousand, mainly from purchases of machinery and tooling); no plant-expansion plan as of the report date. For 2026 the company expects investing outflow from capital expenditures (no separate amount stated); in its investment-policy section, no new investment in investees has been confirmed so far (to be evaluated against production capacity and business needs). Head office and plant in Kaohsiung; its subsidiary STL Energy Technology (S) Pte. Ltd. is the company's R&D center in Singapore. 2026 production policy: assembly of new lithium-ion batteries, more automated production, and readiness for customers' requirements for off-site production. 2026 cash projection: net cash flow from operating activities of NT$(510,532) thousand, primarily from building up inventory and raw materials to fulfill rising customer demand.

items.reason: 'No investment has been confirmed' is from the reinvestment-policy section (investees: STL Investment, STL Corporation, the Singapore R&D unit), not capex; the cash-liquidity analysis says 2026 investing outflow comes from expected capital expenditures, so 'no investment confirmed for 2026' under 'Capex' misstated the source.
items.evidence: Increase in cash outflow from investing and financing activities: Primarily a result of expected investment in capital expenditures and the distribution of cash dividends in the coming year.

items.label: STL Technology annual report: 2025 Annual Report (05-27-2026)
items.signal_prefix: Management risk view: battery cells rely on Japan- and Korea-based suppliers

set.signal: Management risk view: battery cells rely on Japan- and Korea-based suppliers, and with the rapid growth of lithium-ion battery energy storage applications (servers and data centers) cell supply will become tight, while Japanese and Korean cell makers face Chinese manufacturers' cost competitiveness. Responses: cell purchases are set from the year's shipments and major customers' forecasts; negotiating quantities with cell makers relying on its world-renowned customers' group resources may guarantee cell supply even in a cell shortage; because of short supply of active components and battery cells it has prepared materials in advance (raising inventory risk), and if supply of important raw materials becomes tight it will prepare materials in advance at customers' request and sign agreements with customers to repurchase residual materials for certain products.

items.reason: Restore the source's hedges: the customer-resources route 'may guarantee' supply, and the repurchase agreements are a conditional response ('If the supply ... becomes tight'), not a stated current practice.
items.evidence: If the supply of some important raw materials becomes tight due to the emerging electric vehicle market, the Company will also prepare materials in advance per the request of customers
